---
title: "model registries & lineage"
---

## tracking versus a registry

- experiment tracking records runs and their results
- a model registry organises named models and versions, with metadata and references to their originating runs
- lineage connects a model to the data, code, environment, and decisions that produced it
- a registry entry does not by itself deploy a model or establish that it is suitable for use [mlflow registry overview](https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/ml/model-registry/)

::: {.table-responsive tabindex="0"}

| concept | example |
|---|---|
| registered model | `demo-classifier` |
| version | one particular registered artifact |
| alias | a mutable name such as `candidate` pointing to a selected version |
| model signature | the expected input/output structure and optional parameters, used to validate a model’s interface |
| lineage | artifact → training run → code and data versions |

:::

## log a model, then register it

- with mlflow 3 installed, use the same sqlite tracking store as the [tracking example](tracking.qmd)
- this loads the trusted pipeline created by your local lifecycle run, logs it in mlflow model format, and registers a version [registry workflow](https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/ml/model-registry/workflow/)

```python
import joblib
import mlflow
import mlflow.sklearn
from mlflow import MlflowClient

mlflow.set_tracking_uri("sqlite:///mlflow.db")
mlflow.set_experiment("lifecycle-demo")
model = joblib.load("artifacts/run-001/pipeline.joblib")
with mlflow.start_run():
    info = mlflow.sklearn.log_model(model, name="pipeline")
    version = mlflow.register_model(info.model_uri, "demo-classifier")
client = MlflowClient()
client.set_registered_model_alias("demo-classifier", "candidate", version.version)
```

- record the original run id, dataset version, and code revision on this new run so the lineage remains connected
- for a real release, record a model signature, including input names, types, and shapes where relevant; use it to check that inference requests match the expected interface [model signatures](https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/ml/model/signatures/)
- keep the evaluation report, limitations, and intended use with the version
- an alias is mutable; record the resolved version for each deployment rather than relying on the alias name alone [model aliases](https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/ml/model-registry/)

## promote deliberately

- review performance against a baseline, error patterns, relevant subgroups, and inference compatibility
- link the approval decision and responsible owner to the version
- retain the previous version and its environment so rollback, restoring the earlier working release, is possible
- in a bioinformatics workflow, preserve versioned output artifacts and their workflow lineage even when there is no trained model to register
